**6B.6 Research Note: Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2024**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning negative. Tinubu’s 2024 record shows some real crisis-mitigation measures, especially palliatives, dialogue, and targeted support for displaced people and bereaved families. But the biggest 2024 shock, the cost-of-living crisis, still produced mass hardship, food insecurity, and deadly protest repression, so the evidence for broad suffering reduction is incomplete.

**Accepted claims**
- **Nigeria: IMF Executive Board concludes 2024 Article IV consultation / palliatives softened reform shock** | IMF | 2024-02-09 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/09/pr2443-nigeria-imf-exec-board-concludes-pfa)  
  The IMF said Tinubu’s government paired subsidy removal and FX unification with cereals, subsidized fertilizer, a wage award, and diesel VAT suspension. This is strong evidence of active shock mitigation during an economic crisis.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5, 6B.2

- **President Tinubu directs expeditious processing of welfare benefits, demands monthly KPI reports** | State House | 2024-02-22 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/)  
  Tinubu ordered faster welfare delivery and KPI reporting for vulnerable-citizen interventions. That is evidence of trying to reduce avoidable suffering through faster relief delivery.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5, 6B.3

- **President Tinubu calls for suspension of sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso** | State House | 2024-02-24 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/)  
  Tinubu urged “a better path” through negotiation and improved governance rather than punitive escalation. This is indirect but real evidence of de-escalatory crisis management.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

- **President Tinubu establishes comprehensive economic coordination and planning system for Nigeria** | State House | 2024-03-27 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/)  
  PECC/EET put technocrats at the center of emergency economic coordination. This supports a reading of crisis response through structured, expert-driven management rather than improvisation.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5, 6B.4

- **President Tinubu launches national resettlement scheme for conflict victims** | State House | 2024-07-06 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/)  
  The scheme explicitly targeted displaced and conflict-affected communities and framed the effort as rehabilitation and reintegration. This is the clearest direct positive evidence for reducing suffering among crisis victims.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.3, 6B.2

- **President Tinubu launches education campaign: no child should be excluded from learning** | State House | 2024-05-13 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-education-campaign-sys-no-child-should-be-excluded-from-learning/)  
  Tinubu backed girls’ education, anti-GBV policy, and safe schooling for children. This is indirect crisis-relief evidence for vulnerable children and women, though it is more long-run protection than immediate crisis response.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.3, 6B.2

- **President Tinubu approves takeoff of consumer credit scheme** | State House | 2024-04-24 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-approves-takeoff-of-consumer-credit-scheme/)  
  The scheme was framed as helping households finance homes, education, healthcare, and mobility. It is indirect evidence of cushioning economic shock and reducing hardship for ordinary households.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.2, 6B.3

- **President Tinubu offers scholarships, housing to families of slain soldiers** | State House | 2024-03-27 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-offers-scholarships-housing-to-families-of-slain-soldiers/)  
  Tinubu ordered rapid material support for bereaved families, showing the state used direct benefits to reduce suffering after violent loss.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.3

- **President Tinubu acknowledges nationwide protest, hardship, deaths, and destruction** | State House | 2024-08-04 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/)  
  Tinubu publicly acknowledged public frustration, deaths, and destruction tied to economic hardship. This is evidence of recognizing the crisis and trying to manage it politically rather than denying it.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

- **Tinubu asks protesters to suspend demonstrations, seeks dialogue** | TheCable | 2024-08-04 | [URL](https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-tinubu-asks-protesters-to-suspend-demonstrations-seeks-dialogue/)  
  Tinubu explicitly asked protesters to pause demonstrations so dialogue could happen. This is a genuine restraint signal, though reactive and limited.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

- **Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/)  
  Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, and torture during protests over economic hardship. This is the strongest negative evidence that 2024 did not ultimately reduce avoidable suffering during a major domestic crisis.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.3, 6B.5

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- **Hundreds gather across Nigerian cities to protest cost of living crisis** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376)  
  Reuters tied protests to subsidy removal, naira devaluation, electricity tariff hikes, and inflation above 34 percent. This shows the shock response had not yet reduced suffering for many households.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.2, 6B.5

- **Insecurity, rising costs push 31 million Nigerians into acute food shortage, study says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474)  
  The report said 31.8 million Nigerians were acutely food insecure. That is the clearest negative evidence that avoidable suffering remained severe in 2024.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.2, 6B.3

- **Nigeria has detained journalist who reported on corruption in widening crackdown** | Reuters via GPB | 2024-05-09 | [URL](https://www.gpb.org/news/2024/05/09/nigeria-has-detained-journalist-who-reported-on-corruption-in-widening-crackdown)  
  Detaining a journalist over corruption reporting weakens the feedback loop needed to detect suffering and correct policy failures.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

- **Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting** | CPJ | 2024-10-03 | [URL](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/)  
  Continued legal pressure on journalists suggests a punitive information environment, which makes it harder to see and fix avoidable suffering.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

- **Freedom House, Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024** | Freedom House | 2024 | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024)  
  Freedom House describes legal pressure, monitoring, blocking powers, and harassment of journalists. That is negative evidence for transparent crisis correction.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

- **FG spent N63.6bn on military equipment in seven months, report says** | Punch | 2024-08-17 | [URL](https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n63-6bn-on-military-equipment-in-seven-months-report/)  
  Weakly disclosed security spending raises diversion and opportunity-cost concerns during a period of household distress. It does not prove abuse, but it weakens the case that resources were being used to reduce suffering efficiently.  
  QIDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

**Search gap**
- I found direct evidence for **economic shock mitigation, protest dialogue, and conflict-displacement support**.
- I found much less direct evidence for **pandemic response, flood/disaster relief, famine operations, or systematic humanitarian relief coordination** in 2024.
- The strongest negative evidence is outcome-based: **food insecurity, inflation pain, and violent protest repression**, which indicate suffering was still severe despite policy efforts.
